claims.evidence: Lab Tests Online UK (re-retrieved): nothing but water for at least 8 hours, generally 8-10 hours; MedlinePlus: at least 8 hours.
Diabetes UK page: fasting plasma glucose >=7.0 mmol/l (WHO 2006); without symptoms a single result is not enough, at least one additional diabetic-range result on another day is essential.
Diabetes UK: random venous plasma glucose >=11.1 mmol/l. Symptomatic single-result rule corroborated by NHS Highland/South West London guidance. Sentence says 'suggests' so not overstated.
Lab Tests Online UK: at least 8 hours water only. MedlinePlus gives 8-12 h and an NHS OGTT leaflet 8-14 h, so 'at least 8 hours' is the safe common floor.
NICE PH38 glossary: IFG (WHO) is fasting plasma glucose 6.1 to 6.9 mmol/l; Scottish Right Decisions also uses 6.1-6.9 for prediabetes.

NICE PH38: high risk = fasting plasma glucose 5.5 to 6.9 mmol/l (PH38 pairs it with a risk score) or HbA1c 42-47 mmol/mol. MedlinePlus: IFG 100-125 mg/dL = 5.6 to 6.9 mmol/L. Not overstated. Cosmetic: sentence lacks a final full stop.

Diabetes UK: confirmation on another day needed when asymptomatic. Symptomatic single result: retrieved from NHS Highland, South West London ICB guideline and ADA/WHO-based criteria; Diabetes UK's own symptom wording was truncated in the retrieved text, so UK support is by agreement of NHS guidance, not that one page.

Diabetes UK, NHS Scotland, Royal Cornwall (NHS) all: hypo = below 4 mmol/L. NHS 111 Wales page not returned directly. Un-ledgered rest of the pre-existing sentence: 'insulin or tablets' retrieved (sulfonylurea by name not retrieved: textbook); treatment with fast-acting carbohydrate retrieved; 'call 999' not retrieved in this search but is a safe signposting route.
Diabetes UK page: FPG >=7.0; asymptomatic needs another-day confirmation; symptomatic single result adequate per NHS guidance. Jurisdiction UK correct. Value/unit correct.
Diabetes UK: random venous plasma glucose >=11.1 mmol/l; symptoms thirst, polyuria, weight loss match NHS Highland text. UK correct.
Diabetes UK: 2-hour OGTT value >=11.1 mmol/l; 75 g load corroborated by secondary sources. UK correct.
NICE PH38 glossary quoting WHO: IFG 6.1 to 6.9 mmol/l. GLOBAL label is right for a WHO definition (hosted on NICE). 'intermediate hyperglycaemia (prediabetes)' is textbook/standard wording.
NICE PH38 recommendations/glossary: high risk = FPG 5.5 to 6.9 or HbA1c 42-47. UK correct. Note PH38 applies it with a high-risk score; context could add 'together with a high-risk score' (optional).
MedlinePlus: IFG 100-125 mg/dL (5.6 to 6.9 mmol/L); ADA same. US correct.
